tools.name: book_demo
tools.description: Return the calendar URL for a Cargo demo with sales. A person has to pick a time; this tool does not book. Pass email only if they gave an address, never a guess. Use this when someone asks to talk to sales, book a demo, or meet the team. Do not use this to sign in; that is quickstart.

email.description: Work email to prefill the calendar form. Omit if the person did not give an address; never a guess.

tools.name: list_pages
tools.description: Return the llms.txt sitemap: every page of www.getcargo.ai with a one-line description. Use this to discover what pages exist before calling read_page, or to answer questions about what the site covers.

tools.name: open_app
tools.description: Open the Cargo web app in the browser so a person can create a workspace. Pass email only if they gave an address, never a guess. New accounts get free credits and need no card. Do not use this to set up Cargo from a terminal; that is quickstart.

tools.name: quickstart
tools.description: Return the commands to set up Cargo from a terminal: install, sign in (which creates the account), and confirm the workspace. Includes the browser-free --email path. Use this when the caller is an agent or developer in a shell. Do not use this to open the web app; that is the open_app form on the homepage.

tools.name: read_page
tools.description: Read a prose page of www.getcargo.ai as markdown instead of HTML. Use this to answer a question from the site's own words. The home page, blog posts, customer stories and the legal pages answer markdown; product and pricing pages do not, and the tool says so rather than returning their markup. Use list_pages to see what's available.

path.description: Path on www.getcargo.ai, for example "/blog/some-post". Use "/" for the home page, which returns the curated site index.
